searchText: (responding here instead of the other thread) <@372317178906542081> (& cc <@1361003005691822160> & <@394120816461086720> ) great thank you! can y'all be ready to give an update about the state of the problem being fixed for next Thursday's call? iirc there are a few open questions before core devs can even make a decision on it, and we'll need to know whether 8360 is the EIP that's moving forward or another is being written, and whether there are any dependencies. (and as Jochem mentioned, specs/tests would be ideal) > give an update about the state of the problem being fixed Can you elaborate on this? What is actually needed from us ? it would be great if you could take 5 minutes to go over 1. what's being fixed & why 2. what the state of the EIP is 3. if there are any dependencies that need to be added in with 8360. many core devs may be unfamiliar with the EIP and the problem it's addressing, they need to be informed to decide to include it in hegota Ok, I'll joing, <@394120816461086720> joining too? Isn't there a product department in EF that can assist educating the core devs on what ethereum is actually used for? Talked to few ppl and seems the knowledge is scattered and the direction is unclear we'll help on this, 8360 is fixing the bad decision made in glamsterdam, tho would be nice to interact with a dedicated part of the EF that can understand these use cases and what happened such is the nature of decentralized development <:CrazyCry:797948710566625330> the majority of the core devs don't work for the EF and neither do i mhh who took the final decision on what was included in glamsterdam? How this consensus is reached ? I know that many devs and participants don't work for the EF, i'm partecipating as well, tho there's a core team who has the veto EIPs were proposed in a set window last year and then core devs reviewed each and gave their takes on what was most important to be included. the community was encouraged to also review and participate and let AllCoreDevs know what was important (<https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/community-feedback-on-non-headlining-features-in-glamsterdam/26410> & <https://x.com/nixorokish/status/1985807485798924298>) - this was taken into consideration on the calls where the EIPs were discussed. it's extremely helpful when the community chimes in because, yes, core devs don't always have the best visibility to all the use cases onchain. and they're ultimately the ones writing the code and responsible for it, so they do get the final say what would have better gotten your attention / gotten your feedback in that process?

excerpts.content:

Can you elaborate on this? What is actually needed from us ?

excerpts.content: it would be great if you could take 5 minutes to go over 1. what's being fixed & why 2. what the state of the EIP is 3. if there are any dependencies that need to be added in with 8360. many core devs may be unfamiliar with the EIP and the problem it's addressing, they need to be informed to decide to include it in hegota

excerpts.author: nixo.eth
excerpts.content:
EIPs were proposed in a set window last year and then core devs reviewed each and gave their takes on what was most important to be included. the community was encouraged to also review and participate and let AllCoreDevs know what was important (<https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/community-feedback-on-non-headlining-features-in-glamsterdam/26410> & <https://x.com/nixorokish/status/1985807485798924298>) - this was taken into consideration on the calls where the EIPs were discussed. it's extremely helpful when the community chimes in because, yes, core devs don't always have the best visibility to all the use cases onchain. and they're ultimately the ones writing the code and responsible for it, so they do get the final say

what would have better gotten your attention / gotten your feedback in that process?
